::::: {.rblock .area-theory}

:::: {.rblock-text}
### Radiative transfer theory

Vector (polarized) radiative transfer with the matrix-operator adding–doubling method,
linearized analytically so that Jacobians with respect to aerosol, surface and gas
parameters come with the forward calculation. Related work covers first-principles
Cabannes and Raman optical properties of N₂ and O₂, Fourier expansion of Mie scattering
matrices, δ-m and δ-fit truncation for polarized transfer, coupled canopy–atmosphere
transfer, and a semi-analytic 3D framework for oblate, cloudy brown dwarfs.

[Read more →](research.qmd#theory)

### High-performance software

I originally wrote vSmartMOM in Fortran and C++. It is now the open-source Julia package
**vSmartMOM.jl**, whose scientific development I lead. Companion packages provide molecular
absorption from HITRAN and ExoMol, canopy and ocean optics, brown-dwarf and exoplanet
atmospheres, and instrument line shapes. The same code runs on CPUs and GPUs.

[Software and milestones →](software.qmd)

::::: {.rblock .stack .area-earth}

:::: {.rblock-text}
### Earth's atmosphere

The radiance measured from orbit results from scattering by molecules, aerosols and clouds,
line-by-line absorption by trace gases, inelastic Raman scattering, and interaction with the
surface — a vegetation canopy, soil or ocean. My work addresses how these processes affect
retrievals of aerosols, clouds, CO₂, CH₄ and solar-induced fluorescence from instruments such
as OCO-2/3, GOSAT, MISR and SCIAMACHY, including a Raman-scattering correction for SIF
retrievals. I am the radiative transfer lead of the Carbon-I mission concept team.

[Read more →](research.qmd#earth)

:::: {.rblock-text}
### Planets beyond Earth

Photopolarimetric and spectropolarimetric modeling of brown dwarfs and directly imaged
exoplanets. For HWO, multi-epoch ultraviolet observables — lightcurve shape, UV intensity and
polarization colors, and degree of polarization — constrain the scattering state independently
of planetary radius and so address the radius–albedo degeneracy of reflected-light
detections ([Sanghavi, West & Chen 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06649)).

[Read more →](research.qmd#planets)
